hints.title: 1 · Separate rollout from transformation
hints.body: Keep reads compatible with both schemas. Capture a fixed high-water ID and advance over all rows, including skipped records.

hints.title: 2 · Bound each batch before loading
hints.body: Use id > cursor AND id <= high_water, order by id and limit in SQL. Determine done with an existence query after the last scanned ID.

hints.title: 3 · Guard against stale source data
hints.body: Update only if normalized_email is still NULL and email still matches the value you read. Handle only expected uniqueness conflicts.

criteria.title: Safe deployment sequence
criteria.target: Explain expansion, dual-write, backfill, reconciliation, validation and rollback without claiming schema.rb is an online migration.
criteria.probe: What happens if an old writer changes email after the first pass?
criteria.practice: Write a migration rollout and reconciliation plan.

criteria.title: Bounded resumability
criteria.target: Use SQL bounds, a stable high-water mark and a monotonic cursor even on skipped rows.
criteria.probe: Why can filtering NULL rows before choosing a cursor complicate progress?
criteria.practice: Test exact final batches, gaps, retries and new inserts.

criteria.title: Concurrent data preservation
criteria.target: Conditional writes protect both new normalized values and changed legacy inputs.
criteria.probe: Why must the predicate include legacy email as well as normalized_email NULL?
criteria.practice: Interleave a dual-write and legacy-only write between read and update.

criteria.title: Conflicts and compatibility
criteria.target: Preserve legacy data, enforce tenant uniqueness and keep reads compatible without writes.
criteria.probe: How would existing duplicate data affect creation of a PostgreSQL unique index?
criteria.practice: Resolve duplicates before index validation and explain lock duration.

follow_up: Design a reconciliation pass for old writers that still update legacy email after the first high-water run. Define how to distinguish stale normalized values from explicit user edits.
